title: Daily sentences · 2026-08-23

sentences.ko: 그 사람 성격 되게 편한데, 처음엔 좀 조용해. 한 십 분만 주면 금방 풀려. 등산도 엄청 좋아해.
sentences.text: He's easygoing, but he's kind of quiet at first. Give him ten minutes and he'll open up. He's really into hiking too.

alts.text: He's a laid-back guy, a little shy at first, but he loosens up fast. Big into hiking too.
He has an easygoing personality, though he tends to be a bit reserved initially. He becomes more comfortable after a short while. He also has a strong interest in hiking.

sentences.note: **open up** 은 낯을 풀고 편해진다는 뜻입니다. 처음엔 어색해도 시간이 지나면 마음을 여는 사람을 얘기할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 10월 첫째 주 괜찮아? 수요일부터 일요일까지, 사박오일로 생각하고 있어. 빡빡하면 다음 주로 미뤄도 되고.
sentences.text: Can you do the first week of October? I'm thinking Wednesday to Sunday, four nights. If that's tight, we could push it to the following week instead.

alts.text: Free the first week of October? Wed to Sun, four nights. We can bump it to next week if not.
Would the first week of October work for you? I was thinking Wednesday through Sunday, four nights. If that doesn't work, we could move it to the following week instead.

sentences.note: **push it to** 는 일정을 뒤로 미룬다는 뜻입니다. 날짜나 약속을 조정할 때 자주 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 요즘 새벽 세 시쯤 깨서는 천장만 보고 있어. 알람 울릴 때쯤엔 완전히 뻗어 있다니까.
sentences.text: I've been waking up around three every night and just staring at the ceiling. I'm wrecked by the time my alarm goes off.

alts.text: I keep waking up around 3am and just zoning out. I'm dead by the time my alarm goes off.
I've been waking up around three every night and lying there unable to fall back asleep. I'm exhausted by the time my alarm goes off.

sentences.note: **wrecked** 는 완전히 지쳤다는 뜻입니다. 잠을 못 자거나 무리해서 녹초가 됐을 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 응, 일은 그냥 바쁘긴 한데 할 만해. 이번 주에 야근 좀 있었는데 그거 빼면 괜찮아. 걱정하지 마.
sentences.text: Yeah, work's been busy, nothing I can't handle. I've had a few late nights this week, but I'm doing fine. Don't worry about me.

alts.text: Work's just really busy, nothing major. Had a late night or two this week, but I'm good. Don't stress.
Work has been quite busy, but nothing I'm unable to manage. I've had a few late nights this week, but I'm doing well. Please don't worry about me.

sentences.note: **nothing I can't handle** 는 힘들어도 감당할 만하다는 뜻입니다. 부모님을 안심시킬 때 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

sentences.ko: 우리 딸이 이번 학기에 과학 수업을 진짜 좋아해. 현미경 사달라고 계속 졸라. 선생님 말로는 질문을 엄청 많이 한대.
sentences.text: My daughter's really into her science class this semester. She's been begging me to buy her a microscope. Her teacher says she asks a ton of questions.

alts.text: My daughter's totally hooked on science class this semester. She keeps bugging me for a microscope. Her teacher says she never stops asking questions.

My daughter has developed a strong interest in her science class this semester. She has been asking me to purchase a microscope for her. Her teacher mentions that she asks a great number of questions.

sentences.note: **begging me to** 는 계속 조르며 부탁한다는 뜻입니다. 아이가 뭔가를 사달라고 매달릴 때 자연스럽게 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 폰이 갑자기 자꾸 멈춰. 벌써 두 번이나 재시작했는데도 계속 그래.
sentences.text: My phone keeps freezing out of nowhere these days. I've already restarted it twice, but it's still doing the exact same thing.

alts.text: My phone's been freezing randomly. Restarted it twice already, still doing the same thing.
My phone has been freezing unexpectedly. I have already restarted it twice, but the issue persists.

sentences.note: 폰이 버벅거리며 멈출 때 **freezing** 이라고 해요.

sentences.ko: 팟타이 시켰는데 팟씨유가 왔어. 항의 전화하기도 귀찮아서 그냥 내일 다시 시키려고.
sentences.text: I ordered pad thai, but this pad see ew showed up instead. I don't feel like calling to complain, so I'll just order again tomorrow.

alts.text: Ordered pad thai, got pad see ew instead. Can't be bothered calling to complain, gonna just order again tomorrow.
I had ordered pad thai, but I received pad see ew instead. I do not wish to call and complain, so I will simply place the order again tomorrow.

sentences.note: 배달을 다시 시킬 때는 reorder 가 아니라 **order again** 이라고 해요.
sentences.situation: 배달 시켰는데 엉뚱한 게 와서 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 주말 내내 집 밖에 안 나갔어. 그냥 침대에서 뒹굴며 드라마 보는데 딱 필요했던 거더라.
sentences.text: I didn't leave the house all weekend. I just stayed in bed watching shows, and it was exactly what I needed.

alts.text: Didn't leave the house all weekend, just stayed in bed binge watching. Exactly what I needed.
I did not leave the house at all this weekend. I stayed in bed watching shows, and it was precisely what I needed.

sentences.note: 몸도 마음도 쉬고 싶을 때 딱 그거였다는 뜻으로 **exactly what I needed** 라고 해요.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 지난 금요일에 네가 말해준 라멘집 드디어 가봤어. 국물이 진짜 진했는데 기다린 보람이 있더라.
sentences.text: We finally tried that ramen place you told us about last Friday. The broth was so rich, and the wait was actually worth it.

alts.text: Finally tried that ramen place you mentioned last Friday. Broth was so rich, totally worth the wait.
We finally visited the ramen restaurant you recommended last Friday. The broth was very rich, and the wait was genuinely worthwhile.

sentences.note: 고생하거나 기다린 값어치가 있을 때 **worth it** 이라고 해요.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 요즘 회사를 그만둘까 계속 생각하게 돼. 번아웃까진 아닌데 그냥 갇힌 느낌이고, 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: I've been thinking about quitting my job lately. I'm not burned out exactly. I just feel stuck, and I don't know what to do about it.

alts.text: Been thinking about quitting my job lately. Not burned out exactly, just feel stuck and don't know what to do.
I have been considering resigning from my job recently. I am not exactly burned out, but I feel stuck and unsure of what to do.

sentences.note: 완전히 지쳐서 나가떨어진 상태를 **burned out** 이라고 해요.

sentences.ko: 어제 밤에 또 못 참고 피자 시켰어. 맨날 월요일마다 다이어트 다시 시작한다고 해놓고 수요일이면 관둬.
sentences.text: I caved and ordered pizza again last night. I swear I restart this diet every Monday and quit by Wednesday.

alts.text: Yeah, caved again and got pizza last night. I'm serious, every Monday I restart and by Wednesday I'm out.
I gave in and ordered pizza again last night. I attempt to restart this diet every Monday, but I abandon it by Wednesday.

sentences.note: **caved** 는 참으려던 걸 못 참고 무너졌다는 뜻이에요. 다이어트나 결심이 깨질 때 자주 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 들어가자마자 이모가 월급 얼마냐고 물고 늘어졌어. 그다음엔 삼촌이 끼어들어서 결혼은 언제 하냐고 물어보고.
sentences.text: My aunt cornered me about my salary the second I walked in. Then my uncle jumped in asking when I'm getting married.

alts.text: My aunt grilled me about my salary right off the bat, then my uncle piled on with the marriage question.
My aunt pressed me about my salary as soon as I arrived, and then my uncle followed up by asking when I plan to get married.

sentences.note: **cornered** 는 궁지에 몰듯 캐물었다는 뜻이에요. 누가 다그치듯 물어볼 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 명절에 친척들 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 토요일엔 그냥 하루 종일 침대에서 드라마만 몰아보고 집 밖에 안 나갔어. 일요일에야 겨우 일어나서 장 보러 나갔고.
sentences.text: I pretty much binged a show in bed all day Saturday and didn't leave the house. Sunday I finally dragged myself out for groceries.

alts.text: Saturday I just vegged out in bed watching a show all day, didn't budge. Sunday I finally made myself go get groceries.
I spent all of Saturday in bed watching a show and did not leave the house. On Sunday I finally made myself go out to buy groceries.

sentences.note: **binged** 는 드라마 같은 걸 여러 편 몰아볼 때 쓰는 말이에요. **dragged myself out** 은 억지로 몸을 일으켜 나갔다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 이번 주말 이사 진짜 도와주고 싶은데, 언니한테 조카들 봐주기로 벌써 약속해놔서. 다음에 하면 안 될까?
sentences.text: I really want to help you move this weekend, but I already promised my sister I'd watch her kids. Rain check?

alts.text: I'd love to help you move this weekend, but I'm babysitting for my sister already. Next time, okay?
I would really like to help you move this weekend, but I have already committed to watching my sister's children. Could we arrange another time?

sentences.note: **Rain check** 는 지금은 못 하지만 다음에 하자고 청할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

sentences.ko: 어깨가 이상하게 아파서 병원 갔다 왔어. 그냥 자다가 자세가 안 좋아서 그런 거래, 별건 아니고.
sentences.text: I went to the doctor about this weird pain in my shoulder. Turns out I just slept in a bad position, so it's nothing serious.

alts.text: Went to the doctor because my shoulder was killing me. Turns out I just slept funny, nothing to worry about.
I went to see a doctor about some unusual pain in my shoulder. It turns out I simply slept in an awkward position, so it is nothing serious.

sentences.note: **Turns out** 은 알고 보니라는 뜻으로, 결과를 가볍게 전할 때 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

reviewed: 문장 3: "at like three" 의 like 를 장식으로 쓴 채움말이라 십대 말투처럼 들려 around three 로 고쳤습니다.
문장 4: 야근을 extra shifts 로 옮기면 뜻이 달라져(교대근무 느낌) late nights 로 고쳤습니다 (text·formal 모두, casual 문구도 살짝 다르게 조정).
1번 문장의 text 가 19단어로 최소 기준(20단어)에 못 미쳐 자연스러운 표현 "these days" 를 넣어 22단어로 늘렸습니다.
2번 문장의 formal alt 에 축약형 "don't" 가 남아 있어 격식체 기준에 맞게 "do not" 으로 고쳤습니다.
5번 문장의 text 뒷부분이 쉼표로 세 절을 잇는 콤마 스플라이스(comma splice)였는데, 첫 두 절 사이에 마침표를 넣어 문장을 나눴습니다.
2번 문장 formal 에서 cornered 의 다그치는 뉘앙스를 없애고 그냥 asked 로 눅여서 뜻이 순해졌다 — pressed me about 으로 고쳐 압박하는 느낌을 살렸고, note 도 그에 맞게 정리했다.
4번 문장 casual 의 'I'm on kid duty for my sister already' 는 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 어색한 조합이라 자연스러운 'I'm babysitting for my sister already' 로 고쳤다.
